issues.description: Plain-text credit card data in interface. Storing or logging sensitive payment card information (PAN, CVV) violates PCI DSS compliance requirements.
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card details in application code. Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) with tokenization. Accept payment tokens only, never raw card numbers or CVVs.

issues.description: Card validation logic is overly simplistic and insecure. Does not validate card number using Luhn algorithm, does not check for valid card types, and CVV validation is insufficient.
issues.suggestion: Remove all card validation logic from your application. Delegate to PCI-compliant payment processors. If validation is absolutely required, use a vetted library and implement proper Luhn checksum validation.

issues.description: Card number is passed to database layer and potentially logged. Even storing last 4 digits alongside full transaction details can create security vulnerabilities.
issues.suggestion: Use payment gateway transaction IDs instead of card details: await db.query(query, [paymentGatewayTransactionId, amount, 'completed']); Never store, log, or transmit full or partial card numbers unless absolutely necessary and compliant.

issues.description: No error handling or rollback mechanism. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, user is charged but doesn't get the subscription.
issues.suggestion: Implement transaction pattern with compensation logic: try { const paymentId = await chargeCard(...); await upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, paymentId); } catch (error) { await refundPayment(paymentId); throw error; } Consider using database transactions or saga pattern.

issues.description: Expiry date validation has year 2000 bug. 'new Date(2000 + parseInt(year))' will fail for cards expiring in 2100+, and ambiguous date parsing may cause timezone issues.
issues.suggestion: Use explicit date construction and handle year properly: const fullYear = 2000 + parseInt(year); const expiryDateObj = new Date(fullYear, parseInt(month)); Compare year and month separately, not as Date objects.

issues.description: Hardcoded tax rate and processing fee. Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and change over time. Processing fees vary by payment processor and card type.
issues.suggestion: Move tax calculation to a configurable service that determines tax based on user location. Retrieve processing fees from payment gateway configuration. Consider: const tax = await taxService.calculateTax(basePrice, userLocation); const actualFee = await paymentGateway.getProcessingFee(cardType);

issues.description: SQL query is vulnerable to SQL injection if userId is not properly sanitized. While parameterized queries are used, there's no validation of userId format.
issues.suggestion: Validate input parameters before database operations: if (!isValidUuid(userId)) { throw new ValidationError('Invalid userId format'); } Add input validation layer for all user-supplied data.

issues.description: No test coverage for critical payment and subscription logic. This is extremely risky for financial transactions.
issues.suggestion: Implement comprehensive unit and integration tests covering: payment validation, price calculation, subscription upgrades, error scenarios, edge cases (expired cards, insufficient funds), and rollback mechanisms. Target 100% coverage for payment code.

issues.description: Date comparison for expiry validation is incorrect. Comparing full Date objects includes day and time, causing cards to appear expired mid-month.
issues.suggestion: Compare only year and month: const now = new Date(); const currentYear = now.getFullYear(); const currentMonth = now.getMonth(); if (fullYear < currentYear || (fullYear === currentYear && parseInt(month) - 1 < currentMonth)) { return false; }

issues.description: Price calculation does not round to 2 decimal places, leading to floating-point precision errors in financial calculations.
issues.suggestion: Always round currency values: return parseFloat((basePrice + tax + fee).toFixed(2)); Or use a decimal library like decimal.js for precise financial math.

issues.description: Payment errors are logged with console.error, potentially exposing sensitive information in logs.
issues.suggestion: Use structured logging with sensitive data redaction: logger.error('Payment processing failed', { userId, amount, error: sanitizeError(error) }); Never log payment details, card information, or detailed error messages.

issues.description: Feature lists are hardcoded and duplicated. Adding or modifying features requires code changes and is error-prone.
issues.suggestion: Move feature definitions to a configuration file or database: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: [...] }; Or query from database: const features = await featureService.getFeaturesForTier(tier);

issues.description: Subscription validity calculation uses current date without timezone consideration, potentially causing issues for international users.
issues.suggestion: Use UTC consistently: const validUntil = new Date(Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear() + 1, now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate())); Store and compare all dates in UTC to avoid timezone bugs.

issues.description: SQL query uses ON CONFLICT without proper error handling. If the conflict resolution fails, the error is not caught.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit error handling and consider using an ORM for safer queries: try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { if (error.code === '23505') { /* handle unique violation */ } throw new SubscriptionError('Failed to upgrade subscription', error); }

issues.description: Function returns false for both missing subscription and expired subscription, making it impossible to distinguish error conditions.
issues.suggestion: Return explicit status or throw specific errors: if (rows.length === 0) { return { hasAccess: false, reason: 'NO_SUBSCRIPTION' }; } if (validUntil < new Date()) { return { hasAccess: false, reason: 'EXPIRED' }; } This enables better user feedback and error handling.

issues.description: No error handling for JSON.parse. If features column contains invalid JSON, the function will throw and crash.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch for JSON parsing: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON', { userId, error }); return false; }

issues.description: Missing imports and dependencies. The 'db' import from './database' is not validated, and there's no error handling for database connection failures.
issues.suggestion: Add proper dependency validation: import { db, DatabaseError } from './database'; Validate database connection before operations and handle connection errors gracefully.

issues.description: Function lacks proper TypeScript error types and throws generic Error objects, making error handling difficult for consumers.
issues.suggestion: Define custom error types: class PaymentError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public code: string, public details?: unknown) { super(message); } } throw new PaymentError('Invalid payment details', 'INVALID_PAYMENT', { cardNumber: '****' });

issues.description: chargeCard function doesn't use connection pooling or transaction management, potentially causing deadlocks under high load.
issues.suggestion: Use database transactions and connection pooling: const client = await db.getClient(); try { await client.query('BEGIN'); await client.query(query, params); await client.query('COMMIT'); } finally { client.release(); }

issues.description: JSON.stringify is called for every subscription update. For large feature lists, this adds unnecessary overhead.
issues.suggestion: Consider using PostgreSQL JSON columns natively or use a proper ORM that handles JSON serialization efficiently. If using raw queries, batch operations when possible.

issues.description: Functions lack proper JSDoc documentation for parameters and return types, reducing code maintainability.
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc: /** * Gets user's current subscription * @param userId - The unique user identifier * @returns The subscription object or null if not found * @throws {DatabaseError} If database query fails */

issues.description: Payment validation logic is synchronous when it should potentially call external validation services for real card verification.
issues.suggestion: Consider async validation if integrating with real payment processor: async function validatePaymentDetails(payment: PaymentDetails): Promise<ValidationResult> { return await paymentGateway.validateCard(payment.token); }

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES: This code has severe PCI DSS compliance violations by handling raw credit card data (card numbers, CVV). It must use payment tokenization via services like Stripe. Additional critical issues include inadequate error handling causing potential charge-without-subscription bugs, overly simplistic card validation, hardcoded tax/fee calculations, and zero test coverage for financial logic. The code also has multiple date handling bugs, poor error differentiation, missing input validation, and inadequate logging practices. This code should NOT be merged until security issues are resolved, proper payment gateway integration is implemented, comprehensive tests are added, and error handling is improved.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core payment processing function handles financial transactions with no test coverage. Bugs could result in lost revenue, duplicate charges, or unauthorized subscription upgrades.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test suite covering: successful payment flow, invalid payment details rejection, insufficient payment amount rejection, payment gateway failure handling, database rollback on upgrade failure, and concurrent payment processing.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card validation is a security-critical function. Missing tests risk accepting invalid cards, exposing the system to fraud, or incorrectly rejecting valid cards causing customer frustration.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test cases for: valid 16-digit card numbers, invalid card lengths (15, 17 digits), 3-digit and 4-digit CVV validation, invalid CVV lengths, valid expiry date format (MM/YY), invalid date formats, expired cards, cards expiring in current month, and future expiry dates.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date comparison logic has edge cases around month boundaries and year 2000 offset calculation. Could incorrectly validate cards expiring this month or fail on year transitions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test expiry validation for: cards expiring in current month (both beginning and end), cards expiring next month, year boundary transitions (12/24 to 01/25), and year 2099+ edge cases with the 2000 offset.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Pricing calculations directly affect revenue. Incorrect calculations could undercharge customers (revenue loss) or overcharge (legal/reputation issues). No verification of tax and fee calculations.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test exact pricing calculations for: premium tier (9.99 + 8% tax + 2.9% fee = 11.08), enterprise tier (49.99 + 8% tax + 2.9% fee = 55.44), and verify rounding to 2 decimal places for currency.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Direct database interaction for payment recording without tests. Database errors, connection failures, or SQL injection vulnerabilities are undetected. Failure could result in charging cards without recording transactions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: successful charge recording, database connection failures, transaction rollback on errors, SQL injection attempts in card number, concurrent charge attempts, and verify only last 4 digits are stored.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Function returns false on database errors but may have already charged the card externally. No tests verify idempotency or refund handling. Could lead to customer being charged without subscription upgrade.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test error recovery: partial failure scenarios, verify payment gateway is not called if DB is down, test retry logic, and ensure proper transaction boundaries.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription upgrade logic has no tests for feature assignment, date calculations, or database upsert logic. Bugs could grant wrong features or incorrect subscription duration.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: new subscription creation, existing subscription upgrades, downgrade scenarios, feature array correctness for both tiers, 1-year validity calculation, and UPSERT conflict handling.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Adds 1 year to current date without tests. Could fail on leap years, daylight saving transitions, or timezone issues. No verification of subscription duration accuracy.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test date calculations for: leap year boundaries (Feb 29), daylight saving time transitions, different timezones, and verify exactly 365/366 days are added.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Feature access control gates premium functionality. No tests mean authorization bypasses could go undetected. Could allow free users to access paid features or block paying customers.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: user with no subscription (returns false), user with expired subscription, user with valid subscription and correct feature, user with valid subscription but wrong feature, JSON parsing errors, and database query failures.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date comparison for subscription validity has no tests. Edge cases around expiration time (exact second of expiry), timezone handling, or clock skew could grant/deny access incorrectly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test exact expiry boundaries: subscription expires in 1 second, expired 1 second ago, subscription expires today at different times, and timezone differences between server and DB.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription retrieval has no tests for data transformation, null handling, or JSON parsing. Could crash on malformed data or return incorrect subscription details.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: user with no subscription (returns null), user with valid subscription, malformed JSON in features field, invalid date formats, and database connection errors.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Multi-step payment process has no tests for atomicity. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, customer is charged without receiving subscription. No rollback mechanism tested.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test transaction scenarios: charge succeeds but upgrade fails (verify refund/rollback), database transaction boundaries, partial failure recovery, and idempotency for retry scenarios.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Only tests if payment.amount is less than required, but doesn't validate overpayment scenarios. Could accept payments with incorrect amounts or currency issues.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test amount edge cases: exact amount match, overpayment (should this be refunded or accepted?), negative amounts, zero amounts, floating point precision issues, and very large amounts.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Multiple validation checks with early returns. Missing tests could leave validation branches untested, allowing invalid data through or blocking valid data.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Achieve 100% branch coverage with tests hitting: each return false statement independently, all validation passing, and combinations of multiple failures.

untestedPaths.reasoning: All functions depend on imported db module with no integration tests. Database schema mismatches, connection pooling issues, or transaction handling problems are untested.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Create integration test suite with real database: test schema compatibility, connection pooling under load, transaction rollback scenarios, concurrent access patterns, and database migration compatibility.

testCoverage.summary: Critical payment and subscription system with ZERO test coverage. All 6 functions are untested, including security-critical payment validation, financial calculations, and database transactions. High regression risk for revenue-impacting bugs, security vulnerabilities, and data integrity issues. Immediate test implementation required before production deployment.

suggestions.description: Implement the Command or Strategy pattern to separate payment processing steps and improve error handling.
suggestions.before: Function performs multiple responsibilities (validation, pricing, charging, upgrading) in a procedural manner with basic error handling.
suggestions.after: Break into a pipeline of discrete steps (ValidationStep, PricingStep, ChargeStep, UpgradeStep) with proper transaction management and rollback capability.
suggestions.benefits: Better separation of concerns, improved testability of individual steps, easier to add payment processing middleware (logging, auditing), and proper transaction management for payment failures.

suggestions.location: Database query logic in multiple functions
suggestions.description: Extract all database operations into a dedicated repository or data access layer.
suggestions.before: Raw SQL queries are embedded in business logic functions (chargeCard, upgradeUserSubscription, hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription), creating tight coupling.
suggestions.after: Create a SubscriptionRepository and PaymentRepository with methods like savePayment, upsertSubscription, findSubscriptionByUserId. Business logic depends on abstractions, not database implementation.
suggestions.benefits: Improved testability through dependency injection and mocking, easier database migration, better separation of concerns, and adherence to Repository pattern.

suggestions.description: Introduce value objects for sensitive payment data to encapsulate validation and formatting.
suggestions.before: PaymentDetails is a plain interface with string properties, validation happens externally, and sensitive data like cardNumber flows through the system as plain strings.
suggestions.after: Create CreditCard, CVV, ExpiryDate value objects that encapsulate validation in their constructors and provide safe methods (e.g., getLastFourDigits, isExpired).
suggestions.benefits: Impossible to create invalid payment objects, encapsulates validation logic, provides better API for working with payment data, and improves security by limiting exposure of sensitive data.

suggestions.description: Extract card validation logic into separate, focused validation functions for each rule.
suggestions.before: Single function handles multiple validation rules (card length, CVV, expiry format, expiry date) in a sequential if-statement structure.
suggestions.after: Split into focused validators: validateCardNumber, validateCVV, validateExpiryFormat, validateExpiryDate. Use a validation chain or composite pattern.
suggestions.benefits: Each validator becomes independently testable, reusable, and follows Single Responsibility Principle. Easier to add new validation rules and provide specific error messages.

suggestions.description: Implement consistent error handling strategy with custom error types.
suggestions.before: Mix of thrown generic errors, boolean returns, and console.error logging without structured error information.
suggestions.after: Define custom error classes (PaymentValidationError, PaymentProcessingError, SubscriptionError) with proper error codes and details. Use consistent error handling approach.
suggestions.benefits: Better error diagnostics, easier error handling for callers, improved logging and monitoring capabilities, and consistent error response format.

suggestions.description: Extract pricing constants and calculation logic into a dedicated pricing service or configuration module.
suggestions.before: Pricing constants (PRICING, TAX_RATE, PROCESSING_FEE) are hardcoded within the calculateSubscriptionPrice function, making them difficult to modify and test independently.
suggestions.after: Create a PricingConfig class or module to centralize all pricing-related constants and calculations. This enables easier testing, modification, and potential runtime configuration.
suggestions.benefits: Improved testability, easier price updates, separation of business rules from logic, and potential for dynamic pricing strategies.

suggestions.description: Replace conditional feature assignment with a feature mapping configuration.
suggestions.before: Features are assigned using a ternary operator with hardcoded arrays for each tier, duplicating feature definitions.
suggestions.after: Define a TIER_FEATURES constant mapping tiers to their features, or use a feature composition approach where enterprise extends premium features.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplication, makes feature management more maintainable, easier to add new tiers, and enables feature configuration to be externalized.

suggestions.description: Reduce nesting and improve early returns for better readability.
suggestions.before: Multiple nested if statements check subscription existence, validity, and feature inclusion with separate return statements.
suggestions.after: Use early returns with guard clauses and extract subscription validity check into a separate helper function (isSubscriptionValid).
suggestions.benefits: Flatter code structure, improved readability, easier to test individual conditions, and reusable validation logic.

suggestions.description: Use more robust date parsing and validation libraries.
suggestions.before: Manual string splitting and date construction using Date object with hardcoded year 2000 offset.
suggestions.after: Use a date library like date-fns or Day.js for safer date parsing and comparison, or accept ISO date format for better standardization.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces risk of date parsing bugs, handles edge cases better, more readable code, and better timezone handling if needed.

suggestions.location: JSON parsing in hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription
suggestions.description: Extract feature parsing and subscription mapping into helper functions.
suggestions.before: JSON.parse calls are repeated in multiple functions, and row-to-object mapping is duplicated.
suggestions.after: Create parseFeatures and mapRowToSubscription helper functions to centralize data transformation logic.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplication, centralizes error handling for parsing, and makes data transformation more testable and maintainable.

suggestions.description: Remove redundant amount parameter from PaymentDetails interface.
suggestions.before: PaymentDetails contains amount field, but processPremiumPayment recalculates the amount and validates it against the provided amount.
suggestions.after: Remove amount from PaymentDetails and calculate it based on tier. If amount needs to be communicated to caller, return it or use a separate confirmation step.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates confusion about source of truth for amount, reduces potential for amount mismatch bugs, and simplifies the interface.

suggestions.description: Rename to better reflect its actual behavior and return value semantics.
suggestions.before: Function name chargeCard suggests it performs charging, but it actually records a payment and returns success/failure boolean.
suggestions.after: Rename to recordPayment or processAndRecordPayment to clarify that it persists payment information rather than just charging.
suggestions.benefits: Clearer intent, better aligns with actual behavior, and reduces confusion for developers using this function.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file exhibits several critical refactoring opportunities. High-priority issues include tight coupling between business logic and database operations, lack of separation of concerns in payment processing, and primitive obsession with plain strings for sensitive payment data. Medium-priority improvements involve extracting hardcoded configuration values, simplifying validation logic, and reducing code duplication. The file would greatly benefit from applying Domain-Driven Design patterns (value objects, repositories), extracting configuration, and implementing a proper service layer architecture. These refactorings will significantly improve testability, maintainability, and security of the payment processing system.

recommendations.description: Immediately replace raw credit card handling with PCI-compliant payment gateway integration. The current implementation violates PCI DSS requirements by handling plain-text card numbers, CVVs, and expiry dates. Integrate with Stripe, PayPal, or similar tokenization service to accept payment tokens instead of raw card data.

Add comprehensive test coverage for all payment and subscription functions before production deployment. Zero test coverage on financial logic creates unacceptable risk of revenue loss, data corruption, and transaction failures. Implement unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end payment flow tests with minimum 95% coverage.

Implement proper transaction rollback and compensation logic for payment processing. Current code can charge users without granting subscriptions if upgradeUserSubscription fails. Add database transactions, implement refund mechanism, and use saga pattern or two-phase commit to ensure atomicity.

Extract all database operations into dedicated repository layer to improve testability and separation of concerns. Raw SQL queries embedded in business logic create tight coupling and make unit testing difficult. Create SubscriptionRepository and PaymentRepository with proper abstractions.

Implement custom error types and consistent error handling strategy throughout the module. Current mix of thrown errors, boolean returns, and console logging makes debugging difficult and prevents proper error recovery. Define PaymentError, ValidationError, and SubscriptionError classes with error codes.

Extract hardcoded pricing, tax rates, and feature lists into external configuration. Current hardcoded values require code changes for business rule updates and cannot adapt to different jurisdictions or pricing tiers. Move to database or configuration service.

Fix multiple date-related bugs including year 2000 offset issue, incorrect expiry comparison, and timezone handling problems. Use explicit UTC date handling and compare year/month separately. Consider using date-fns or similar library for robust date operations.

Add comprehensive input validation for all user-supplied data including userId format validation, amount validation, and parameter sanitization. Implement validation layer before database operations to prevent injection attacks and data integrity issues.

Introduce value objects for payment data (CreditCard, CVV, ExpiryDate) to encapsulate validation and prevent invalid state. Current primitive string handling allows invalid data to propagate through the system and violates domain-driven design principles.

Replace console.error with structured logging that redacts sensitive information. Current logging may expose payment details and create security vulnerabilities. Implement proper observability with sanitized logs, metrics, and alerts for payment failures.
